tasks.name: dev_pipeline.py _label_issue helper + label tracking
tasks.description: Add _label_issue(issue_number, labels, repo) helper using _run_gh. Modify claim_issue() to add 'dev:in-progress' label. Modify create_pr() to change to 'dev:pending-review' label via --add-label/--remove-label. _label_issue catches subprocess errors (non-fatal if label missing).
tasks.notes: Label names (dev:in-progress, dev:pending-review) use colon separator matching GitHub label convention. Labels must exist in repo or gh fails silently — non-fatal.
tasks.implementationGuide: 1. Add _label_issue(issue_number, labels, repo=DEFAULT_REPO) → calls _run_gh(['issue', 'edit', str(issue_number), '--repo', repo, '--add-label', ','.join(labels)]) 2. In claim_issue(), after successful assign: _label_issue(issue_number, ['dev:in-progress']) 3. In create_pr(), after PR created: _label_issue(issue_number, ['dev:pending-review']); remove dev:in-progress via _run_gh with --remove-label 4. Wrap each in try/except for non-fatal label failures
tasks.analysisResult: DevForge Devin-like pipeline label tracking + governance tier + systemd timer. dev_pipeline.py already has gh CLI wrapper (_run_gh) and state persistence. cli.py has dev subcommand. Systemd timer pattern exists in devforge-day-cycle.
tasks.summary: _label_issue helper added with add/remove label support via _run_gh. claim_issue() adds dev:in-progress after assign. create_pr() swaps dev:in-progress → dev:pending-review. All wrapped in non-fatal try/except.

tasks.name: cli.py dev poll --auto-safe --claim flags
tasks.description: Add --auto-safe flag to dev poll subparser (filters to auto-safe issues). Add --claim flag that auto-claims all polled issues. Implement auto-claim loop in cmd_dev_poll.
tasks.notes: --claim without --auto-safe claims ALL unassigned issues. Usually used together: --auto-safe --claim.
tasks.implementationGuide: 1. dev_poll.add_argument('--auto-safe', action='store_true') 2. dev_poll.add_argument('--claim', action='store_true') 3. In cmd_dev_poll: if args.auto_safe: issues = poll_issues(auto_safe=True) 4. If args.claim: for i in issues: ok = claim_issue(i['number']); print result. Add counter at end.

tasks.name: systemd timer/service for auto-safe polling
tasks.description: Create devforge-dev-poll.service (ExecStart=cli.py dev poll --auto-safe --claim --once) and devforge-dev-poll.timer (OnCalendar=*:0/10). Enable timer.
tasks.notes: Type=oneshot + OnCalendar=*:0/10 follows same pattern as devforge-day-cycle. No Restart= needed for oneshot.
tasks.implementationGuide:
1. Write ~/.config/systemd/user/devforge-dev-poll.service: [Unit] Description=DevForge Dev Poll — auto-safe issues claim
[Service] Type=oneshot ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 /opt/projects/server/scripts/cli.py dev poll --auto-safe --claim --once WorkingDirectory=/opt/projects/server/scripts 2. Write ~/.config/systemd/user/devforge-dev-poll.timer: [Unit] Description=DevForge Dev Poll 10min timer
[Timer] OnCalendar=*:0/10 Persistent=true
[Install] WantedBy=default.target 3. systemctl --user daemon-reload 4. systemctl --user enable --now devforge-dev-poll.timer 5. Verify with systemctl --user list-timers
tasks.analysisResult: DevForge Devin-like pipeline label tracking + governance tier + systemd timer. dev_pipeline.py already has gh CLI wrapper (_run_gh) and state persistence. cli.py has dev subcommand. Systemd timer pattern exists in devforge-day-cycle.
